shorts.title: What you will learn: stack, queue and deque
shorts.hook: Last in, first out. First in, first out.
shorts.script: Last in, first out. First in, first out. Today we meet two simple containers with strict rules. One is a pile of plates, and the other is a queue at a shop. A stack is last in, first out. You push on top, and you pop from the top. A queue is first in, first out. You push at the back, and you pop from the front. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: stack, queue and deque.

shorts.title: stack, queue and deque in one minute
shorts.hook: A stack is last in, first out.
shorts.script: A stack is last in, first out. You push on top, and you pop from the top. A queue is first in, first out. You push at the back, and you pop from the front. A deque lets you push and pop at both ends. Think of a pile of plates for the stack, and a line at the ration shop for the queue. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: stack, queue and deque in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Asha joins the queue first. Meera joins last. Front shows Asha, the first in line. Pop removes Asha. Now Ravi is at the front, and Meera is at the back. The program prints Asha, and then Ravi Meera. A stack is last in, first out. A queue is first in, first out. Top and front only look. Pop removes. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Expecting pop to return the item
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in stack, queue and deque?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in stack, queue and deque? Bug of the Day. We store the result of pop in an int. The compiler says void value not ignored as it ought to be. Pop returns nothing. First read with top, then remove with pop. Pop returns nothing. This design keeps the stack safe when an exception happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Expecting pop to return the item.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you reverse a word with a stack in stack
shorts.script: Can you reverse a word with a stack in stack, queue and deque? The stack was proud. It said, I am always on top of things. Use a stack of chars to reverse the word Goa. Push each letter, then pop them all. Write your answer in the comments. A stack is last in, first out. A queue is first in, first out. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
